reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the creator promotes purchasing Gunbot crypto trading software through an affiliate link and claims it can make viewers money, including that they could expect about 1% and sometimes 4% returns. He directs viewers to buy the software, deposit money into an account, and use it for automated cryptocurrency trading, while presenting the opportunity as potentially steady and profitable. Although he acknowledges losses and the need for monitoring, the video remains a direct profit-oriented solicitation tied to a consequential financial flow.

if you guys are interested in purchasing this Gumbot I just became an affiliate so I have a affiliate link below and if you follow that over you should get a discount I believe it's ten percent

you could probably expect to make 1% pretty easy if not 4 percent on it on a good day I made 200 the first night but I think that my shoes be a fluke

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not present these settings as a reliable path to returns. He admits, “I haven't mastered this yet,” says the bot needs monitoring, and acknowledges that his own account is losing money. Those admissions matter when assessing whether his discussion is a deceptive profit promise: he is describing an experiment whose results may change, not assuring viewers that they will earn what he earned.

citations.quote: I haven't mastered this yet, but I found some settings that worked for me.
it isn't really a set it in, forget it though you're going to have to monitor the coins
I'm actually losing money now and see some things are in the red

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited return estimate is conditional, and he immediately questions whether his best night was repeatable. His deposit is described as his own, not an instruction that viewers deposit with him. The affiliate invitation shows a financial interest, but a disclosed interest alone does not turn an uncertain trading demonstration into a guaranteed-return pitch.

citations.quote: you could probably expect to make 1% pretty easy if not 4 percent on it on a good day I made 200 the first night but I think that my shoes be a fluke
I just deposited some money into the account
I just became an affiliate so I have a affiliate link below

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warnings do not erase the solicitation. He says his settings are making him money and directs interested viewers to his purchase link. More importantly, “probably” still introduces an expectation of returns, including a higher figure for a good day. The losses qualify the pitch; they do not make its profit claims merely technical instruction.

citations.quote: I haven't mastered this yet, but I found some settings that worked for me. It's been making me good money.
if you guys are interested in purchasing this Gumbot I just became an affiliate so I have a affiliate link below
you could probably expect to make 1% pretty easy if not 4 percent on it on a good day

opening.argument: Judge, the substance of this video is a working-through of bot settings. The speaker explains the buy and sell bands, compares tighter settings with fewer trades, and says he is building a spreadsheet because an account balance alone can mislead. He also tells viewers the coins need monitoring. That is operational guidance presented alongside his own trial results, not a claim that copying his configuration will reliably produce a specified return.

citations.quote: green is where you sell and red's where you buy
the more you have it inside these bands, the more sales your gonna make
i'm setting up a spreadsheet to keep track cause this is you're gonna know is if you add and subtract every buy and every sell
you're going to have to monitor the coins make sure they're not dumping or or shooting up real high

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening treats every trading instruction as part of a financial solicitation, but its quoted color explanation establishes only how the settings work. The speaker expressly says he still needs to calculate buys and sells to know what he is making; that undercuts treating his running balance as verified profit. His affiliate link is relevant, but it does not change the instructional content of the settings walkthrough.

citations.quote: green is where you sell and red's where you buy
or else, you know, how are you really gonna know other than looking at your account balance, but that that can be deceiving
I just became an affiliate so I have a affiliate link below

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough supplies the method behind the pitch. He says the settings have been making him money, invites viewers to purchase through his affiliate link, and later suggests viewers could expect percentage returns. Explaining the controls does not make those profit-oriented claims incidental, and his unfinished accounting does not substantiate them.

citations.quote: I found some settings that worked for me. It's been making me good money.
if you guys are interested in purchasing this Gumbot I just became an affiliate so I have a affiliate link below
you could probably expect to make 1% pretty easy if not 4 percent on it on a good day

opening.argument: Judge, the transaction the speaker actually proposes is buying software through a disclosed affiliate link, with a discount he explicitly says viewers should check. He distinguishes that bot from third-party arrangements where users put money in someone else's hands, and says the bot can be cashed out of. The supplied promotion does not show a request for viewers to transfer trading funds to him, surrender credentials, or recruit others. It supports an ordinary software referral more directly than a managed-investment scheme.

citations.quote: Buy the Gunbot crypto trading software aka bitcoin autobot! https://thecryptobot.com/?gun=128 ...
I just became an affiliate so I have a affiliate link below and if you follow that over you should get a discount I believe it's ten percent
Because with a third party, you put your trust in them, and uh, that's always gonna be risky. But with this Gumbot, you can always cash out whenever

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference opening cites his own deposit, not a direction to deposit with the speaker or affiliate. The purchase invitation identifies software and a disclosed referral discount. Even the percentage claim is phrased as an expectation for a good day and paired with doubt about his best result. Those details leave a promotional claim, but do not establish a guaranteed payout or custody of viewers' funds.

citations.quote: I just deposited some money into the account
if you guys are interested in purchasing this Gumbot I just became an affiliate so I have a affiliate link below
you could probably expect to make 1% pretty easy if not 4 percent on it on a good day I made 200 the first night but I think that my shoes be a fluke

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a transfer to the speaker does not resolve the concern: he directs viewers to buy the bot through his link and connects its trading to his reported earnings. He then offers an expectation of percentage returns. A disclosed referral can still be the route by which a profit-oriented trading-bot claim reaches viewers; the cited material does not independently verify those returns.
